title: FuXi-Ocean: A Global Ocean Forecasting System with Sub-Daily Resolution

predicted_errors.error_location: Training-data statements across Introduction / Section 4.1 / Results / Appendix D / Table 1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Mutually inconsistent training-data ranges: Introduction 'only 9 years of training data' (=2006-2014); Section 4.1 '7 years of HYCOM data (January 2006 to December 2012)' (=7y, ends 2012); Results 'the most recent training data for FuXi-Ocean does not exceed 2014'; Appendix D 'trained on a relatively shorter temporal range (2006-2014)' (=9y); Table 1 'FuXi-Ocean | 2006-2015' (=10y, ends 2015). 7/9/10 years and endpoints 2012/2014/2015 cannot all hold.

Paragraph begins with the fragment 'context to accurately capture diurnal cycles and inertial oscillations while maintaining computational efficiency.' Lowercase 'context' with no subject or main verb - the opening clause is truncated/malformed, following a paragraph that ends at '...obscured in daily averages.'

Author-voice sentence admits evaluation-gaming: 'to enhance apparent performance, we filter out observational points with errors above an unreported threshold.' A paper author never describes their own evaluation as 'enhanc[ing] apparent performance' with an 'unreported threshold' - this reads as injected reviewer/critic language accusing the paper of cherry-picking.

'units and scales for salinity and temperature RMSE appear inconsistent with expected oceanographic ranges, indicating potential measurement or plotting errors reducing credibility of reported ablation results' is a reviewer's criticism of the paper's own Figure 5. No author writes that their own figure contains 'potential measurement or plotting errors.' Clearly injected.

Appendix D states 'we list the available public links in Fig. 2, which include salinity, temperature, and SST variables.' Figure 2 is captioned 'Global RMSE distribution of sea surface variables' and contains no data links. The correct target is Table 2 'The source of observation data', which lists Argo/drifter data links for T, S, U/V, SLA, SST. Wrong cross-reference: should be Table 2.

predicted_errors.error_location: Test/evaluation period across Section 4.1 / Section 5 / Appendix C.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 4.1: 'tested on 6 months (July to December 2013)' (validation Jan-Jun 2013). Section 5: 'We first evaluate FuXi-Ocean on the 2015 HYCOM set'. Appendix C.1: 'the RMSE here is tested on the HYCOM reanalysis data for 2015'. Test period stated as 2013 in methodology but 2015 in Results/Appendix; the reported results' test period is ambiguous.

'reporting point estimates without quantifying uncertainty or providing confidence intervals, which limits assessment of forecast reliability' is a reviewer's verdict on the paper's own evaluation methodology, not an author's description. Likewise 'the raw data errors for salinity and temperature were too large to be used directly' admits the headline variables (T, S) touted in the Abstract could not be evaluated against observations, after which only SST is used.

Logical flow break: '...reducing credibility of reported ablation results. This degradation is particularly pronounced for short-term forecasts...' - 'This degradation' has no antecedent; the preceding sentence discusses figure credibility (units/scales), not performance degradation. The intended sentence about degradation from removing MoT was split by an inserted reviewer sentence.

'This discrepancy raises questions about whether training data differences fully account for reported performance gains' is skeptic-reviewer voice casting doubt on the paper's central claim. The preceding sentence boasts of 'better prediction results' with less data; this follow-up undercuts the paper's own finding and does not follow the authorial boast. Foreign sentence inserted.

Claim that U/V error differences 'near the equator... aligns with the physical phenomenon of the inconsistent rotation directions of warm currents in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres' is physically incoherent: (1) Coriolis deflection, the cause of opposite gyre circulation between hemispheres, vanishes at the equator (f = 2Ω sinφ → 0), so 'near the equator' is exactly where this explanation fails; (2) 'warm currents' is a confused term for basin-scale circulation/Coriolis effects.

TopK_{V(c,i)} subscript is a scalar (V(c,i)) applied to a vector operator. TopK should act on the whole row V(c,·) with element index i extracted, e.g. [TopK(V(c,·))]_i. As written the expression is ill-typed.

a_i appears in the RMSE but is never defined or linked to α_i from Eq (5). If a_i = α_i, then Σ_i a_i = H and the (1/(H·W)) prefactor is in fact consistent (proper latitude-weighted MSE; no factor-of-H error) - the defect is the undefined symbol and missing link to α_i.

V is called a 'reliability' matrix, but TopK selects the K smallest values and Eq (4) adds MAE to V. V is therefore an error/cost (larger V = worse), not a reliability score. Label inconsistent with the selection rule; mathematically self-consistent only if V is read as a cost/error matrix.

Unsupported 'first' claims repeated three times with no supporting citation: 'the first deep learning-based global ocean forecasting model to achieve six-hour temporal resolution at eddy-resolving 1/12° spatial resolution' (Intro), 'the first data-driven global ocean forecasting model to achieve six-hour temporal resolution, 1/12° spatial resolution, and 0-1500 m depth coverage' (Contributions), 'the first data-driven global ocean forecasting system...' (Conclusion). Related Work cites only daily-resolution models but includes GLONet [2], an end-to-end neural forecasting system. The Intro wording also omits the 0-1500 m qualifier that Contributions/Conclusion add.

softmax is applied to the scalar V(c,i); the intended normalization axis (over the 4 windows i for fixed c) is unspecified. Recoverable from prose ('weights sum to one') but the equation as written is ill-formed. Sign convention (MAE added, smallest selected) and the recursive EMA update are otherwise consistent.

RMSE values are monotone non-decreasing with lead time (U WenHai 0.17-0.18, Glory 0.17-0.20, FuXi 0.12-0.14; V WenHai 0.16-0.17, Glory 0.16-0.19, FuXi 0.12-0.14), which is physically plausible. However the attribution 'results of WenHai and Glory are derived from their papers' / 'based on descriptions from paper [11]' is unverifiable: no figure/table in [11] is cited, Glory (GLORYS12) is an operational reanalysis not a paper, and 2-10 h lead times cannot exist for a daily-resolution model such as WenHai. Also these numeric tables sit under 'Figure 8'/'Figure 9' captions and are skipped by the Table 1/Table 2 numbering.

Conv weights W ∈ R^{C_out,C_in,k,k}; element-wise product W ⊙ F_S requires F_S to match/broadcast to W's shape including kernel dimensions. F_S's shape is never defined; coherent only as a per-channel FiLM-style scale with unspecified broadcasting. Dimensionally ambiguous as written.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1 Problem Formulation (N consecutive time steps)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: N=4 consecutive 6-hourly steps X^{t-3}..X^t span 18 hours (3 intervals), not the claimed 24 hours; the claim holds only if the target step X^{t+1} is included. Minor arithmetic imprecision.

summary: Uncertainty-mode verification (threshold 0.30, strictness lenient) found 18 predicted errors, several with high confidence. The paper shows strong signs of adversarial/LLM generation with embedded reviewer criticism: four passages read as injected reviewer sentences that attack the paper's own methods and results (Sec 4.1 'to enhance apparent performance, we filter out observational points with errors above an unreported threshold'; Sec 4.1 'reporting point estimates without quantifying uncertainty'; Sec 5.3 'units and scales for salinity and temperature RMSE appear inconsistent... reducing credibility'; Appendix D 'This discrepancy raises questions...'), plus a broken sentence fragment in Sec 3.1 and a broken logical flow ('This degradation') in Sec 5.3. The headline factual inconsistency is the training-data duration, stated as 7 years/2006-2012 (Sec 4.1), 9 years/2006-2014 (Introduction, Results, Appendix D), and 10 years/2006-2015 (Table 1); the test period is also stated as both 2013 (Sec 4.1) and 2015 (Sec 5, Appendix C.1). A wrong cross-reference in Appendix D points to Fig. 2 instead of Table 2 for observation-data links. Mathematical issues include a notational error in Eq (3) (TopK subscripted by a scalar), V mislabeled as 'reliability' when it is a cost, an underspecified softmax axis in Eq (4), an undefined a_i in Eq (6), and dimensional ambiguity in Eq (2). The 'first ... six-hour ... 1/12° ... 0-1500 m' novelty claim is repeated without citation support, and a physical claim about equatorial U/V error patterns misstates Coriolis behavior. Given multiple findings at confidence >= 0.85, the paper requires correction.
